items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen after dinner. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes seems to be enough to get most of the benefit, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Eating dinner late, at 8 pm or later, is linked to a rise in sugar, with dinners from 8-9 pm linked to a rise about 13.3 mg/dL more than dinners before 6 pm. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it makes a difference for you.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 11.7 hours, and 0.0% of nights reached 13 hours. In the randomized program, adding the overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points (95% CI -0.06 to 0.0) compared with coaching alone. It looked larger in some blood sugar groups, but the program could not tell the groups apart, so this is the overall number. A check in real people (NHANES) showed no clear link yet.

rejected.text: Having an overnight fast, where you don't eat for a certain number of hours, is being studied to see if it helps with sugar. Your overnight fast averaged 11.7 hours, and you might consider trying to reach 13 hours to see if it makes a difference for you.
